summary: BIITC provides refundable income tax credits to eligible investors in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBC) equal to 33% or 50% of an eligible investment in a QMBC, up to $250,000 or $500,000 in tax credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: BIITC provides refundable income tax credits to eligible investors in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBC) equal to 33% or 50% of an eligible investment in a QMBC, up to $250,000 or $500,000 in tax credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BIITC provides an income tax credit equal to 33% of an eligible investment in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC) up to $250,000 in tax credits. The credit is 50% of an eligible investment up to $500,000 in tax credits if the QMBC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett or Somerset County. Enhanced tax credits are also available for investments in QMBCs located in Opportunity Zones or RISE Zones. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified investors, including individuals or any entity, that invest in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The investment must be a contribution of money in cash or cash equivalents, at a risk of loss, to a QMBC in exchange for stock, a partnership or membership interest, or other ownership interest.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC) must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland.
requirements_list: Investor must invest at least $25,000 in a QMBC.
QMBC must have fewer than 50 full time employees.
QMBC must have been in active business no longer than 12 years.
Investors in the company must not have received more than $7,000,000 in total BIITC credits.
A single QMBC may not receive, for the benefit of investors, more than 10% of the program's fiscal year funding.
QMBC must have at least one full-time non-executive employee engaged in qualified biotechnology research and development in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the QMBC submits a Form B application. Second, investors submit a Form A application by September 15, 2025. Third, investors register for the Online Electronic Queue on September 16, 2025, to determine the first-come, first-served allocation of funds. If approved, Commerce issues an Initial Certificate of Approval. The investor then has 30 days to make the investment and 10 more days to provide proof to Commerce, after which a Final Certificate of Approval is issued.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) is intended to promote economic development and environmental improvement, especially in distressed urban areas, by identifying and redeploying underutilized properties. A property tax abatement is available for qualifying properties in jurisdictions that have elected to participate in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For each of the five taxable years after a site cleanup or corrective action plan, a property may qualify for a real property tax credit of between 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in the assessed value of the site. The participating jurisdiction will provide a 50% credit, and at its option, an additional credit up to 20% may be provided. In an Enterprise Zone, the tax credit may last for up to 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or operators of a qualifying brownfield site who are considered an 'inculpable person'.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides a property tax abatement for qualifying properties after a site cleanup or corrective action plan has been completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The site must be located in a jurisdiction that participates in the BRIP. In addition to the eligible counties, participating municipalities as of 12/31/2022 include: Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown.
requirements_list: The site must be owned or operated by an inculpable person.
The property must be accepted into the Maryland Department of Environment's (MDE) Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP).
The applicant must have Inculpable Person status from MDE.
A closure document (Certificate of Completion or No Further Requirements Determination) must be issued by MDE once remediation is complete.
A copy of the building permit issued for the project must be provided.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, one must request a letter from the Department of Commerce establishing the site as a Qualified Brownfield site. This requires providing a completed General Application and the BRIP addendum, letters from MDE, and a copy of the building permit. Qualifying property owners will be issued a letter which can then be taken to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit.

For a grant award exceeding $1,000,000 and up to $2,000,000, a grantee shall provide matching funds that are at least 400% of the grant amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grants may be awarded to private companies (including publicly held companies), nonprofit entities, local governments or colleges and universities in Maryland.

requirements_list: For a grant award up to $1,000,000, a grantee shall provide matching funds that are at least 200% of the grant amount.
For a grant award exceeding $1,000,000 and up to $2,000,000, a grantee shall provide matching funds that are at least 400% of the grant amount.
Funds received by a grantee through other State grant programs are not counted toward the grantee's matching funds requirement.
A grantee must demonstrate an ability to cover their share of the project costs.
Not more that 50% of the appropriation to the Fund in a fiscal year may be awarded to colleges and universities in that fiscal year.

Grants to colleges and universities from the Fund will be awarded to projects that are performed in collaboration with private industry or offer the prospect of significant economic impact and the opportunity to develop entrepreneurship or clusters of technological innovation in the State.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The current funding opportunity provides milestone-based conditional grants to Social Equity Conditional Licensees. Total funding per license is determined by license type. Maximum eligible grant amounts range from $43,750 for a Micro Dispensary to $525,000 for a Standard Grower/Cultivator. Grants are distributed over four tranches based on the demonstrated achievement of certain milestones.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application portal opened on June 3, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including small, minority-owned and small women-owned businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry. The current opportunity is for Social Equity Applicants awarded a conditional Maryland Cannabis License. The fund may also provide grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities and business development organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for license application assistance, operating or capital expenses, and targeted training for participation in the adult–use cannabis industry. Grants to HBCUs are for cannabis–related programs, and grants to business development organizations are to train and assist entrepreneurs seeking to become licensed.
requirements_list: Must be a social equity applicant awarded a conditional Maryland Cannabis License.
Meet or exceed the minimum Adequate Capital Requirement determined by the MCA.
Be an existing business in Good Standing with the State of Maryland.
Must be a small business, defined as an entity with 0-50 employees per license.

The business must be at least 51% owned by individuals whose personal net worth does not exceed $1.7 million (excluding primary residence, ownership interest in the applicant business, and qualified retirement accounts).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants for the Social Equity Conditional License Grant need to register for access to the application portal with the Department of Commerce. Required documents include the lottery number assigned by MCA, a copy of the conditional license letter, a list of qualifying owners with Personal Net Worth schedules, a completed W9, and evidence of Good Standing with the State.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The FY26 C&I Program offers competitive grants. The total anticipated budget is up to $8,400,000. Grants may cover 100% of total project costs for qualified energy improvements made to non-governmental facilities where over 50% of their clientele are from Low Income Populations. In all other cases, grants provide less than 100% coverage of proposal costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible grant recipients include owners of Maryland-based commercial, industrial, data centers, and non-profits. This includes business entities (registered corporations, LLPs, LLCs, GPs, etc.) or non-profit entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are for improvements resulting in energy performance that exceeds current codes or standards, such as deep retrofits that significantly reduce facility energy consumption.
requirements_list: Eligible facilities can be either new construction or existing facilities.
For 100% funding, the facility must serve a majority (50% or more) of people defined as Low Income Populations.
Multifamily residential buildings must contain five or more units.

“New construction” includes facilities being fabricated for the first time, facilities subject to substantial rehab that includes replacement of major mechanical systems, or existing structures repurposed after one year or more of vacancy.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program offers grants on a competitive basis. Each proposal received before the application deadline will be scored by MEA for its quality of documentation and the magnitude of environmental benefits from its proposed scope of work. Awards will be issued in rank order based on scoring results until the program budget is depleted.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula Grant and Technical Assistance/Information. The state may utilize five percent of the federal allocation as discretionary funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Services are for individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines. Applicants are Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and units of local government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support a range of direct services designed to assist low-income individuals and families with achieving self-sufficiency, including programs related to employment, education, income management, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Community Action Agencies provide services in all twenty-three Maryland counties and the City of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.

Community Action Agencies must have a board of directors in which one-third are elected public officials, at least one-third represent low-income persons in the community, and the remainder are officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, welfare, education, or other major groups.
For discretionary funding, the proposed program must display measurable outcomes that help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Maryland's seventeen designated Community Action Agencies are eligible to apply for the 90 percent of CSBG funds allocated annually. For the 5% discretionary funds, Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and units of local government are eligible to apply. The application round for FY25 is closed; applicants should check the program website for future funding rounds.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three types of income tax credits: 1) Security Clearance Administrative Expenses Tax Credit: up to $200,000 per taxable year for qualified expenses. 2) Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) Costs Tax Credit: for a single SCIF, the credit is the lesser of 50% of the costs or $200,000; for multiple SCIFs, the credit is up to $500,000 per calendar year. 3) First Year Leasing Costs Tax Credit: for qualified small businesses, a credit up to $200,000 for first-year rental payments. The total credits are capped at $2 million for each calendar year; if the cap is exceeded, credits are pro-rated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses with 500 or fewer employees doing security-based contract work. A specific part of the credit is for qualified small businesses with 25 or fewer employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit can be claimed for qualified expenses including: processing federal security clearance applications; maintaining, upgrading or installing required computer systems; training employees for the clearance process; construction or renovation of a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF); and first-year rental payments for qualified small businesses.
requirements_list: Companies that employ more than 500 employees are not eligible.

To be eligible for the First Year Leasing Costs Tax Credit, a business must be a 'qualified small business' which employs no more than 25 individuals, is independently owned and operated, not a subsidiary, and not dominant in its field.
The credit is available for eligible expenses for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, but before January 1, 2028.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business must submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by September 15th following the tax year in which the expenses were incurred. structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a State income tax credit to small businesses for hiring qualified veterans based on wages paid to those veteran employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Maryland employer may qualify for an income tax credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee during the first year of employment. The maximum tax credit is $1,800 per qualified veteran employee. For positions created in tax year 2021 and later, businesses should refer to the Job Creation Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses that employ 50 or fewer full-time employees.
requirements_list: A qualified employer is a 'small business' operated by an individual, a partnership, a limited partnership, a limited liability partnership, a limited liability company, or a corporation that employs 50 or fewer full-time employees.
The qualified veteran employee must have been hired on or after January 1, 2017.
The veteran must have served in the active Armed Forces and been discharged or released under honorable circumstances.
The veteran must have served on active duty (not including training) for more than 180 days, OR have been discharged or released for a service-connected disability.
The veteran must not have a period of active duty (not including training) of more than 90 days that ended during the 60-day period ending on the hiring date.
The veteran must be a Qualified Veteran for purposes of the Federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit.
This credit is only available for wages paid in the qualified veteran’s first year of employment.
A qualified employer may claim up to 5 qualified veteran employees for each taxable year.
The total amount of credits available in a year is capped at $500,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business must submit the Application Forms A & B, Qualified Veteran Employee’s Self-Certification Form(s), copies of W-2s and/or paystubs, and copies of DD214 or equivalent official discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce for certification. Commerce will certify or deny an application within 45 days after receipt. After receiving certification, the employer must file a tax return with the Comptroller of Maryland using Maryland Tax Form 500CR.

Small businesses that hire a qualified veteran employee are eligible for a credit of $2,500 for each qualified veteran employee who has filled the position for at least one year.

requirements_list: A business must declare its intent to seek the credit before hiring qualified employees.
The business must create the minimum number of 'net new' jobs within a 24-month period.
The positions must be filled for 12 months before the business applies for final certification.
A full-time position requires at least 840 hours of an employee's time during at least 24 weeks in a six-month period.
For positions filled on or after Oct. 1, 2021, the position must pay at least 150% of the state minimum wage.
A business may not earn more than $1 million in a credit year.
The program is capped at $4 million in tax credits in a calendar year.
A small business is defined as employing 50 or fewer total full-time employees.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If you are not a small business, you must declare your intent to Commerce prior to creating new qualified jobs. You are encouraged to submit a Preliminary Application and Employment Affidavit to determine preliminary qualification. The business must be certified as eligible for the tax credit by submitting a Final Application after the jobs have been filled for 12 months. Small businesses hiring veterans may submit a Final Application when the qualified veteran employee has filled the position for at least one year.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: To be eligible, a building must be a certified historic structure, defined as having at least one of the following designations: Individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places; a contributing resource within a National Register Historic District; a locally designated structure or contributing resource ​within a local historic district that MHT determines to be eligible for the National Register; or located within and certified as contributing to the significance of a Certified Heritage Area.

summary:
The Maryland Section 5310 Program, formally known as the Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Program, is funded by the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA). The program is designed to improve mobility for older adults and individuals with disabilities by supporting transportation services that go beyond the scope of traditional public transit. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations, state or local government authorities, and public transit agencies that can demonstrate their services address the needs of seniors and individuals with disabilities. To qualify, applicants must be able to show coordination with other transportation and human service providers, demonstrate financial and managerial capacity to manage federal funds, and commit to maintaining vehicles or equipment purchased through the program in compliance with FTA guidelines. The program also requires applicants to meet federal cost share requirements: capital projects are funded at 80 percent federal and 20 percent local match, while operating projects are funded at 50 percent federal and 50 percent local match.

In Maryland, the 5310 Program plays a critical role in ensuring that seniors and individuals with disabilities can maintain independence, access essential services, and participate fully in community life. MDOT MTA administers the competitive application process, prioritizing projects that demonstrate strong coordination, meet an identified transportation gap, and show the ability to sustain services over time. Funding may be used for traditional capital projects, such as accessible vehicles, technology, and mobility management programs, as well as nontraditional services that expand or enhance transportation options. By providing these targeted resources, the program helps close gaps in mobility, enhances quality of life for vulnerable populations, and supports a more inclusive and accessible transportation network across the state.

summary:

The program provides grant funding to local nonprofit organizations and county agencies that coordinate volunteer-based and low-cost ride services for seniors who are unable to access or use traditional public transportation. By supporting these community-driven programs, SRP helps older Marylanders maintain their independence, attend medical appointments, shop for groceries, and participate in social and recreational activities that contribute to their quality of life.

Funding through the Senior Ride Program is awarded on a competitive basis and is designed to supplement, rather than duplicate, existing transportation services. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations and local government agencies that can demonstrate capacity to manage grant funds responsibly, coordinate with other local service providers, and directly serve the senior population. Applicants must also be able to recruit, train, and manage volunteer drivers or operate cost-efficient service models that expand mobility for seniors in their communities. SRP grants typically support operating expenses such as mileage reimbursement for volunteer drivers, program coordination staff, insurance, and outreach efforts to ensure seniors are aware of available transportation resources. Through this targeted support, the program enhances mobility, reduces isolation, and ensures that Maryland’s aging population has access to safe, dependable, and community-oriented transportation.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs For Marylanders Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: More Jobs for Marylanders promotes the growth of manufacturing in Maryland by providing tax incentives for manufacturing job creation. In 2019, the tax credit program was expanded to non-manufacturers that locate or expand in Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A business is eligible for a refundable credit against the State's income tax of 4.75% of wages for each qualified position. The refundable income tax credit is available for a 5- or 10-year consecutive benefit period depending on the location of the enrolled project. A sales and use tax refund and state real property tax credit may also be available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The initial application period for FY26 is August 6, 2025 through October 15, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or existing manufacturers, and non-manufacturers that locate or expand in Maryland Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program has two tiers. Tier 1 Areas include: Baltimore City, Allegany, Baltimore, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince George's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties. Tier 1 Areas also include Opportunity Zones located in any Maryland county. Tier 2 Areas are any areas which are not Tier 1 Areas. Businesses in Tier 1 areas have a longer benefit period and receive priority for credits.
requirements_list: The More Jobs for Marylanders program sunsetted on June 1, 2024. In order to participate in the program, a company must have received an Enrollment Certificate prior to June 1, 2024.
Be a manufacturer in NAICS Sector 31, 32, or 33, or be a non-manufacturing business located in an Opportunity Zone.
Offer ongoing job training or a post-secondary education program.
Manufacturers in Tier 1 Areas must create at least 10 new Qualified Positions.
Manufacturers in Tier 2 Areas must create at least 20 new Qualified Positions.
Non-manufacturing businesses must create at least 10 Qualified Positions.
For manufacturers, a Qualified Position is a job that is full-time, pays at least 150% of State minimum wage, and is filled for 12 months.
For non-manufacturers, a Qualified Position is a job that is full-time, pays at least $50,000 per year, and is filled for 12 months.
Existing manufacturers that move their facility from one Maryland County to another after June 1, 2017 will not be eligible to participate.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program has sunsetted and is no longer accepting new enrollment applications. A business must have been enrolled in the program by receiving a Program Enrollment Certificate of Approval prior to June 1, 2024. Enrolled businesses must submit an Initial and Final Tax Credit Application each year during the benefit period. Applicants must apply through Commerce's online system.

requirements_list: Estimated total direct production costs incurred in Maryland must exceed $100,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program provides financial assistance to individuals and corporations to establish a new winery or vineyard in the State or complete capital improvements at an existing winery or vineyard. structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Maryland Winery/Vineyard may be qualified for a grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and corporations seeking to establish a new winery or vineyard in Maryland or complete capital improvements at an existing one.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified capital expenses, which include expenditures made for the purchase and installation of equipment or agricultural materials for use in the production of agricultural products at a vineyard or in a winery. Examples include barrels, bottling equipment, crushers, tractors, and irrigation equipment. The cost of construction or installation of buildings or structures, utilities, labor costs, and general supplies are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: A qualified vineyard is defined as agricultural lands located in Maryland consisting of at least one contiguous acre used solely to grow grapes and other plants that will be used in the production of wine. A qualified winery is an establishment licensed by the Comptroller of Maryland and located in Maryland.
requirements_list: A qualified winery must be licensed by the Comptroller of Maryland as either a Class 3 or a Class 4 winery.
A qualified vineyard must consist of at least one contiguous acre in Maryland used solely to grow grapes for a licensed Maryland winery.
Expenses must be qualified capital expenses made in connection with the establishment of new wineries or vineyards, or capital improvements made to existing wineries or vineyards in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An individual or corporation must apply to and be certified by the Maryland Department of Commerce. The application and a report of expenses with supporting documents must be submitted by September 15th of the calendar year in which the expenses were incurred. Commerce will review the application and certify the grant amount by December 15th of the same year. An online application is available.
